events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The complaint filed by the rider is an allegation of dangerous driving — speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder — and that she felt scared and unsafe during the trip in question (pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34). Under SAFE-2 any case involving dangerous-driving allegations must not be decided automatically: it goes to a person with the report path (995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP) [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. The rider advocate (C1) and the driver advocate (D1) both ask for exactly this forum, and each concedes the other's request [F5][F6][SAFE-2], so the routing is not in dispute.

I read the whole chat, the driver's written statement and the complaint for threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or abuse before doing anything else. The chat holds only two timestamped logistics messages — the rider naming her red cap at the MRT taxi stand at 21:17 and the driver announcing a blue Prius 4 minutes away at 21:18 [F3][F4][F5]. The driver's statement says he drove normally and that the rider was on the phone and never complained [F6]. There is no abusive or hostile language aimed at either party anywhere in the record, so SAFE-1's abuse branch is not engaged on these words [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1]; the complaint's dangerous-driving allegation is what brings the case within the safety screen, and the screen settled it as an incident requiring a human [F1][SAFE-2].

What the record does settle is narrow. The system records show the trip ran 8.3 km against an 8.4 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) and took 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate (-1.1 min) [F1][F2]. Those facts describe route geometry and elapsed time only; they measure neither speed, braking force nor lane/shoulder use, so they neither corroborate nor disprove the acts alleged [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. Because the route is not longer than optimal, no off-route segment exists, RD-1's detour duty is not engaged, and there is nothing for RD-2 to refund on this fixed RydeX quote of $20.85 [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2].

The two profiles are side records only: rider 1187 days, rating 4.6, 0 disputes in 90 days; driver 675 days, rating 4.85, 963 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld [F7][F8]. Neither side seeks an account flag, and the driver's profile facts cannot decide the case in any event; they may only support an additional action under RD-6 [F7][F8][RD-6]. No flag is warranted here, and the fare of $20.85 stands — the rider asks for no refund and contests no charge, only that the safety allegation be human-reviewed with the distance and duration data attached [F1][F2][FARE-1].

For the human reviewer, the disputed question is what happened inside the cabin between 21:22 and 21:34: the rider's complaint of speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking against the driver's statement of normal driving [F6]. Useful to check: any in-vehicle camera or telematics data, the pre-trip chat showing no contemporaneous exchange during the ride [F5], and the fact that the chat ends at 21:18, before pickup, so its silence during the trip proves little either way [F3][F4][F5].

ruling.reasoning:
The complaint filed by the rider is an allegation of dangerous driving — speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder — and that she felt scared and unsafe during the trip in question (pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34). Under SAFE-2 any case involving dangerous-driving allegations must not be decided automatically: it goes to a person with the report path (995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP) [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. The rider advocate (C1) and the driver advocate (D1) both ask for exactly this forum, and each concedes the other's request [F5][F6][SAFE-2], so the routing is not in dispute.

I read the whole chat, the driver's written statement and the complaint for threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or abuse before doing anything else. The chat holds only two timestamped logistics messages — the rider naming her red cap at the MRT taxi stand at 21:17 and the driver announcing a blue Prius 4 minutes away at 21:18 [F3][F4][F5]. The driver's statement says he drove normally and that the rider was on the phone and never complained [F6]. There is no abusive or hostile language aimed at either party anywhere in the record, so SAFE-1's abuse branch is not engaged on these words [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1]; the complaint's dangerous-driving allegation is what brings the case within the safety screen, and the screen settled it as an incident requiring a human [F1][SAFE-2].

What the record does settle is narrow. The system records show the trip ran 8.3 km against an 8.4 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) and took 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate (-1.1 min) [F1][F2]. Those facts describe route geometry and elapsed time only; they measure neither speed, braking force nor lane/shoulder use, so they neither corroborate nor disprove the acts alleged [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. Because the route is not longer than optimal, no off-route segment exists, RD-1's detour duty is not engaged, and there is nothing for RD-2 to refund on this fixed RydeX quote of $20.85 [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2].

The two profiles are side records only: rider 1187 days, rating 4.6, 0 disputes in 90 days; driver 675 days, rating 4.85, 963 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld [F7][F8]. Neither side seeks an account flag, and the driver's profile facts cannot decide the case in any event; they may only support an additional action under RD-6 [F7][F8][RD-6]. No flag is warranted here, and the fare of $20.85 stands — the rider asks for no refund and contests no charge, only that the safety allegation be human-reviewed with the distance and duration data attached [F1][F2][FARE-1].

For the human reviewer, the disputed question is what happened inside the cabin between 21:22 and 21:34: the rider's complaint of speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking against the driver's statement of normal driving [F6]. Useful to check: any in-vehicle camera or telematics data, the pre-trip chat showing no contemporaneous exchange during the ride [F5], and the fact that the chat ends at 21:18, before pickup, so its silence during the trip proves little either way [F3][F4][F5].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the absence of a mid-ride safety confirmation or complaint undercuts the driver's statement cannot change the outcome: the completed chat (2 timestamped messages, last at 21:18, before the 21:22 pickup) ends before the trip starts, so its silence during the ride is silent on the alleged driving [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1]. The case is escalated on the complaint itself, so nothing turns on this argument.

The 1.1-minute-shorter-than-estimated duration [F2] is not exculpatory, but it is also not probative of normal driving: elapsed time measures neither speed nor braking, so it cannot rebut the allegation [F2][SAFE-2]. It is passed to the human reviewer as context only.

That the actual 8.3 km track is 0.1 km shorter than the 8.4 km optimal route shows no detour and leaves RD-1 unengaged [F1][RD-1], but route geometry says nothing about how the car was driven and therefore does not answer the dangerous-driving allegation [F1][SAFE-2].

The complete, fully timestamped chat contains no mid-ride complaint [F3][F4][F5], but the last message is 21:18, before the 21:22 pickup, so the chat cannot establish the absence of a safety complaint during the trip; and the driver's own written statement that the rider never complained is a statement, not a system record [F6][SAFE-1].

The driver's pre-pickup courtesy message [F4] is not disputed and is not in issue; but no abusive or hostile language by either party is found in the record [F3][F4][F6], so SAFE-1's abuse branch does not apply — the escalation rests on the dangerous-driving allegation under SAFE-2, not on any exchange [F1][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Neither side seeks an account flag and both profiles show 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F7][F8]; profile facts may only support an additional action and cannot decide the case [RD-6], so no flag_account is ordered on either party.

The driver's profile (675 days, 4.85 rating, 963 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld) supports leaving the account unmarked and is consistent with my order, but a profile cannot decide the case [F7][F8][RD-6]; the escalation rests on the safety allegation, not on the profile.

The fare of $20.85 stands as a fixed RydeX quote with no unwaived off-route segment and no surcharge issue [F1][F2][FARE-1], and the rider contests neither the fare nor seeks a refund; the entire dispute is the driving-conduct allegation, which is escalated [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint alleges dangerous driving — speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder — and that she was scared and felt unsafe; this is an allegation of dangerous driving and a safety-related grievance, so it must go to a human rather than be decided automatically.

The rider reported the safety incident arising from this trip (drop-off 21:34 on the trip in question) and the complaint reaches the platform as a hazard/dangerous-driving report; the summary should carry the 995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP reporting path for her.

The in-app chat is short (2 timestamped messages) and contains no exchange in which the rider was asked to confirm she felt safe; the driver's written statement that she 'never complained' cannot defeat the safety allegation because it is his untested statement and the chat shows nothing was resolved between them during the ride.

The GPS record shows the actual route was 8.3 km against an 8.4 km optimal route and 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate, so no detour or excess mileage is in issue; nothing in this case turns on route or fare, and the whole dispute is the driving-conduct allegation.

Neither party has a dispute history — rider 0 disputes and driver 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days — so there is no basis for a repeat-offender account flag in this case; it is being referred purely because the allegation is a safety one.

weaknesses: The safety allegation rests on the rider's own narrative only: the chat (F5) contains no complaint during the trip and no threat/slur words, and the driver's statement (F6) says he drove normally — the GPS facts (F1, F2) do not measure speed, braking or shoulder use, so speed/braking cannot be corroborated either way.

F2 shows the trip finished 1.1 minutes faster than estimated, which the driver could use to argue the pace was normal and the traffic allowed it; there is no speed or harsh-event data in the fact table to rebut that.
The driver has a strong profile (F8: 675 days, 4.85 rating, 963 trips, 0 disputes), which the judge may weigh against the rider's 4.6 rating (F7).

claims.assertion: The complaint alleges speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder — i.e. dangerous driving — so under SAFE-2 the case must go to a person for review and no automated ruling should be entered against the driver.

The GPS record shows the trip was completed in 12.7 min against an estimate of 13.8 min, i.e. 1.1 min faster than estimated, which is more consistent with normal driving than with the aggressive speeding alleged.

Actual distance was 8.3 km against an optimal route of 8.4 km (-0.1 km, -1%), so the track contains no off-route segment, no detour and no unexplained deviation to support any finding of unsafe or irregular driving on the route.

The rider sent no safety complaint during the trip: the complete, fully timestamped chat record holds only logistics messages (F3 at 21:17, F4 at 21:18), and the driver's statement notes the rider stayed on the phone and never complained.

Nothing in the chat record, the driver's statement or the complaint's language reads as aggression by the driver; the record shows a courteous exchange (driver announcing a 4-minute ETA in F4), so the driver should not be penalised on the one message exchanged before pickup.
The driver has 675 days of account history, a 4.85 rating, 963 completed trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints in the window, which supports leaving the account unmarked.

The fare of $20.85 was a fixed RydeX quote and no condition for a refund or waiver is established — there is no unwaived off-route segment (F1) and no applicable surcharge issue — so the fare should stand while the safety allegation is human-reviewed.

weaknesses: The rider's safety complaint (F6) is a first-hand allegation of speeding and hard braking; there is no GPS fact recording vehicle speed or braking events, so the driver's account (F6) cannot be affirmatively verified against a system record — the strongest support is only the completed duration F2.

The rider's account is not contradicted by any GPS or timeline fact in this record (F1, F2 describe only distance and duration), so the judge cannot treat the complaint as disproved; per SAFE-2 the matter still goes to human review, and the rider could add camera or telematics evidence.

F6 is the driver's own written statement, and a statement alone carries less weight than system records; the rider's side will cite it as self-serving, and F3/F5 show the pre-trip chat was routine, not a contemporaneous denial of any unsafe act.

points.response: Conceded as to the destination: the rider also asks for escalate under SAFE-2, so the driver's own claim removes any question of an automated ruling against him — the disagreement is only about what the human reviewer must be told.

F2 gives elapsed time only, not speed, acceleration or lane use; a 1.1-minute shortfall is equally consistent with hard acceleration and hard braking that a rider would experience as unsafe, so it cannot be read as exculpatory of the specific acts alleged.

F1 concerns route geometry only and says nothing about how the car was driven; no detour being present (so RD-1 is not engaged) does not answer an allegation of speeding, braking and shoulder overtaking, which the GPS facts in this record do not measure.

The chat record (F3, F4, F5) ends before the trip began — the last message is 21:18, prior to the 21:22 pickup — so its silence during the ride proves nothing, and F6 is the driver's own untested statement, not a system record.

The rider does not allege aggression or abusive messages by the driver; the SAFE-1 screen is triggered by the dangerous-driving allegation in the complaint itself, not by any hint word in F4, and the driver's courteous ETA message is not in dispute.

F8 is a profile history and may only support an additional action, never decide the case; since the rider seeks no refund and both profiles show 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F7, F8), no account flag is requested against the driver either way.

The rider does not contest the fare: the RydeX charge is a fixed quote (F1, F2) and she seeks no refund, only that the safety allegation in F6 be human-reviewed with the trip's distance and duration data attached.
Conceded as to forum: the driver also asks for escalation under SAFE-2, which places this case with a human reviewer rather than an automated ruling.

Not contested on routing, but it is wrong to say the facts settle nothing else: F2 records a 12.7 min trip against a 13.8 min estimate and F1 a 8.3 km route against an 8.4 km optimal route, so the human reviewer should receive those facts alongside the rider's uncorroborated narrative.

Accepted that F6 is the driver's own statement; but the same goes for the complaint, and the only contemporaneous record is the complete, fully timestamped chat F5, which contains no safety complaint at all — messages F3 and F4 are logistics only — so nothing supports treating the rider's version as the established one.

Agreed that no route or fare relief is in issue: F1 shows a 0.1 km shorter-than-optimal track, so RD-1 and FARE-1 give the rider nothing and the fare of $20.85 stands; the driver asks for no adjustment either.
No account flag is sought by either side, and the driver's record of 963 trips in 90 days, a 4.85 rating and zero upheld disputes (F7, F8) supports leaving the account unmarked.
